content.summary_of_the_paper: This work proposes APPROVED, an unsupervised detection mechanism to detect adversarial examples. Specifically, APPROVED attempts to detect out-of-distribution behavior in the logit layer via “data depth” to detect adversarial examples. The authors evaluate APPROVED on deep neural networks (ResNet) and Vision Transformers (VIT) and show that their method achieves higher detection methods than previous unsupervised detection methods.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
## Strengths
(+) The detection of adversarial examples is an important research topic toward the robustness and generalization of adversarial examples.  
(+) To the best of my knowledge, this is the first work that leverages “data depth” to detect adversarial examples.  
(+) This is one of a few works which investigate the detection of adversarial examples on vision transformers.  

## Weaknesses
(-) Previous works have demonstrated that most adversarial detection techniques can be fooled [A, B, C, D], e.g. due to obfuscated gradients. While the authors dedicate Section 5.2 “Adaptive Attacks” to that topic, unfortunately, they brush off the most important part: the evaluation of white-box adaptive attacks. The authors justify this with the statement that “finding a differentiable surrogate of IRW remains a very challenging open research question”. At least a more fine-grained discussion is required to justify this claim. Ideally, the authors would also demonstrate that the approximation of the non-differentiable part through a neural network (or other techniques) indeed fails.  
(-) [B, C] provide guidelines for the evaluation of new adversarial defense techniques. The authors should have followed & discussed these guidelines.  
(-) It seems that the proposed technique is only applicable to ViTs. I am wondering if this phenomenon is only observed for this specific ViT architecture? Since the authors only evaluate ViT it is not clear if this is a general observation for transformer architectures? Additionally, I am wondering about the data depth values of other standard architectures, such as DenseNet, Inception, or MobileNet?  
(-) Regarding white-box attacks, I would like to note that AutoAttack is the current best practice to evaluate white-box attacks.  
(-) In Figure 1 it appears that the STA attack is ineffective for ViT. I might have missed it, but I couldn’t find an explanation for this. Could the authors elaborate on this phenomenon? 

[A] Adversarial Examples Are Not Easily Detected: Bypassing Ten Detection Methods; AISec’17  
[B] Obfuscated Gradients Give a False Sense of Security: Circumventing Defenses to Adversarial Examples; ICML 2018 
[C] On Evaluating Adversarial Robustness; arXiv 2019  
[D] Detecting Adversarial Examples Is (Nearly) As Hard As Classifying Them; ICML 2021 workshop
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
## Clarity
This work is clearly written and technically sound to the best of my judgment.

## Quality 
The paper quality is sufficient in my opinion. 

## Novelty
The idea of detecting adversarial examples with “data depth” is novel to the best of my knowledge. 

## Reproducibility
This work is reproducible (code provided) to the best of my judgment.
content.summary_of_the_review: While the idea of detecting adversarial examples with “data depth” appears to be novel, in my opinion, the authors did not attempt a best-effort attack on their defense technique. It has been shown several times in the literature, that most adversarial defense techniques can be broken, e.g. due to obfuscated gradients. In my opinion, newly proposed defense techniques should clearly provide evidence that they are resistant to white-box adaptive attacks. This work fails to provide such evidence.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 5: You are absolutely certain about your assessment. You are very familiar with the related work and checked the math/other details carefully.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The paper proposes an adversarial examples detection method based on the logit information obtained from the network on the input images. The proposed approach claimed to be computationally efficient and hard to break by the gradient-based approaches. The experiments are performed on three datasets and two attacks.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
The proposed approach shows success in defending the old adversarial attacks compared to earlier adversarial examples detection methods.

- The proposed paper is far behind the current literature. The paper makes claims which are false and not properly defended such as (i) detection has received low attention (ii) VGG and ResNets are more explored. 

[1] Aldahdooh A, Hamidouche W, Fezza SA, Déforges O. Adversarial example detection for DNN models: A review and experimental comparison. Artificial Intelligence Review. 2022 Jan 6:1-60.

The following authors alone have presented several detection methods, the other detection methods can also be found in the comparisons and the survey paper mentioned above.

[2] DAMAD: Database, Attack, and Model Agnostic Adversarial Perturbation Detector, In IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems (IEEE T-NNLS), 2021

[2b] Image Transformation based Defense Against Adversarial Perturbation on Deep Learning Models, In IEEE Transactions on Dependable and Secure Computing (IEEE T-DSC), 2021

[2c] Detecting and Mitigating Adversarial Perturbations for Robust Face Recognition, In International Journal of Computer Vision (IJCV), 2019

The proposed algorithm needs to be evaluated against recent and state-of-the-art attacks including black box, non-gradient-based, and adaptive attacks. 

The comparison is also performed with old-age defense algorithms. The paper needs significant updates in its literature. 

The generalizability in detecting unseen attacks also needs to be addressed. The authors can refer to several generalization scenarios outlined in [2a][2b]. 

The average values of the performance are reported which makes it hard to understand where the approach is failing or passing. What is the limitation of the proposed algorithm?

No visualization of data depth and how it is relevant to be used for detection. 

No supporting evidence of the low computational cost: time, FLOPs, etc.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The paper needs significant updates in its literature and experimental setup. 

The novelty is hard to comment on in the absence of incomplete literature. 

As per the paper, the source codes are provided for reproducibility.
content.summary_of_the_review: The paper lacks depth in presenting the current research defending the adversarial attacks. The majority of its setup is old and no state-of-the-art components are used. Due to these facts, the contribution of the proposed paper is very limited and has little impact in defending the adversarial examples.

content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 1: The contributions are neither significant nor novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focuses on designing a new detection method for adversarial examples. As a detection strategy, the paper suggests using a statistical concept, i.e., the data depth, as a similarity measure. The proposed detection method computes the data depth of logit output, then by thresholding the data depth, an adversarial example can be filtered out. On the experimental side, the authors measured the detection performance on the vision transformer. The authors first delve into the vision transformer’s behavior to justify that the proposed method is well-suited for the vision transformer. Then, the authors evaluate the detection performance against various attacks on the vision transformer.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
[[Strengths]]
1. The authors evaluated the performance against various attacks, and the result supports the apparent improvement in adversarial example detection.
2. Section 4 provides valuable insights into the vision transformer’s behavior compared to ResNet18’s behavior. It is worth exploring what causes the difference between the vision transformer and ResNet18.
3. The authors know the potential adaptive attacks and evaluate the detection performance. Particularly, based on existing works about depth score approximations, the authors well-explained why BPDA, one of the most common adaptive attacks, cannot be a valid attack against their method.
4. Circumventing the proposed detection methods reduces to a challenging open problem of approximating the data depth. This may motivate the research regarding data depth, opening more potential applications of data depth to the field. Therefore, this work may earn more significance for encouraging future work.

[[Weakness]]
1. Section 4.3 demonstrates why the evaluation is made specifically for the vision transformer, using the logit layer. However, isn’t it also important to perform some assessment on ResNet18 to show the performance on the model that does not go along with the idea?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The authors’ contributions look novel, and the writing is straightforward and understandable.
content.summary_of_the_review:
I consider this paper acceptable for many reasons.
1. data depth looks like a useful concept, even for other defense methods.
2. the experimental exploration of the target models’ behavior provides valuable insights into those models. 
3. the authors evaluated the performance against many different attack methods
4. the experimental results demonstrated an impressive performance compared to existing detection methods.
5. The performance does not degrade against adaptive attacks, and white-box adaptive attack is challenging for the proposed method.
content.correctness: 4: All of the claims and statements are well-supported and correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 4: The contributions are significant, and do not exist in prior works.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: In this work, the authors propose a novel scheme for the detection of adversarial examples, based on the statistical measure called data depth. In particular, the authors seek to utilize a Monte-Carlo approximation of the Integrated Rank-Weighted (IRW) depth computed with respect to the logit predictions of the training distribution, in order to define a scoring function that detects adversarial examples based on a set-threshold.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
1) The notion of data depth revisited by the paper specifically toward analyzing the nature of logit predictions is indeed interesting.
2) The paper also analyses the case of detection for the case of Vision Transformers (ViTs), while much of the existing literature is focused towards ResNet based architectures, since it is the hitherto default for comparative analysis in the field. 



Weaknesses:
1) The experimental evaluations presented have several aspects of concern. For example, the paper states that the non-differentiability of the IRW based data depth makes it difficult for gradient-based attackers to target the proposed method. Indeed, obfuscated gradients do not provide any robustness or security by themselves — it only makes it difficult for attackers to find adversaries, and implies nothing about their non-existence. That is, though adversarial examples might be difficult to find, the defense can be extremely susceptible to changing predictions for several input points within the assumed threat model. 
2) Thus it is imperative to evaluate the attacks using smooth approximations such as BPDA as a minimal, necessary baseline. Though section 5.2 states “Whitebox attacks (e.g. BPDA (Athalye et al.,2018)) are not straightforward to adapt in our case since finding a differentiable surrogate of IRW remains a very challenging open research question in the statistical community”, the proposed defense cannot be evaluated in a fair manner without the same. Given that most of the evaluations presented rely upon gradient-based attacks, we naturally expect the specific attacks considered (eg. FGSM, BIM, PGD, DeepFool) to be extremely weak against the proposed method. However for non-differentiable detectors, these are insufficient to establish robustness metrics. Furthermore, standard black-box attacks such as Square and Spatial Transformations are not good baseline attacks for detection methods since these often have distribution specific features, and moreover do not target the detection method itself in any manner. Thus, the results so presented do not truly imply that the proposed method is effective in practice.
3) Indeed, several such defenses that benefit from gradient obfuscation have been broken [1], and do not provide any reliable measure of robustness or security. Furthermore, Carlini et al [2] show that distribution based detectors can be bypassed fairly easily using fine-tuned adaptive schemes that specifically target the defense, and present overarching guidelines on how detection based defenses need to be carefully evaluated. Without such adaptive evaluations, the efficacy of the detection method cannot be established in a valid manner. Given the large number of detection based defenses compromised, the paper needs to establish that the proposed defense is robust against the attacks that were found to compromise these similar past works as a requisite baseline, alongside new adaptive attacks specifically crafted for data-depth based detection.
4) More recently, Bryniarski et al. [3] present Orthogonal Projected Gradient Descent, wherein detection based defenses are compromised using orthogonalised gradients to simultaneously satisfy the constraints of misclassifying the network while being undetected. The authors further break four state-of-the-art detection defenses using the same method. Indeed in the paper, the broken detection techniques such as Dense Layer Analysis (section 5.2) and Sensitivity Inconsistency (section 5.3) are similar to the use of data-depth as a statistical measure, and are likely to extend to the current defense at hand as well, and needs to be included to serve as a baseline evaluation. 
5) The main comparisons presented are limited to Feature Squeezing and MagNet, which are fairly outdated. Indeed, Feature Squeezing and was broken as a detection defense by He et. al [4], and does not serve as a good detection baseline. Indeed, several stronger baselines have been established, though several have been compromised as in [3]. Thus, the proposed method out-performing Feature Squeezing, which was broken as a detector, does not yield a reliable indicator of the robustness achieved. 
6) The proposed method appears to iterate through the entire training set for each inference step, with the overall complexity given by O(N*n*d) where N refers to the number of Monte Carlo samples used, n is the size of the dataset, and d is the dimension of the logit layer. This appears to create a severe limitation during inference time, and is quite difficult to utilize in several practical scenarios.
7) Furthermore, the detection defense is shown to achieve extremely high rates of robustness for large perturbation radii such as epsilon=0.5 for L-infinity based attacks (Tables-6,7,8 of Appendix). However Tramer [5] shows that given a detector for adversaries at radius epsilon, a robust classifier can be constructed against adversaries at radius epsilon/2. This thus serves as a sanity check to test whether the detection rates presented are stronger than they really are. In this case, this would imply the existence of a robust classifier at radius epsilon=0.25 for L-infinity adversaries, which appears to be extremely strong and is unexpected.

Minor Typo on Page3: “relaxe” -> ”relax”


[1] Obfuscated Gradients Give a False Sense of Security: Circumventing Defenses to Adversarial Examples, Anish Athalye, Nicholas Carlini, David Wagner
[2] Adversarial Examples Are Not Easily Detected: Bypassing Ten Detection Methods, Carlini et al., 2017
[3] Evading Adversarial Example Detection Defenses with Orthogonal Projected Gradient Descent, Oliver Bryniarski, Nabeel Hingun, Pedro Pachuca, Vincent Wang, Nicholas Carlini, 2021
[4] Adversarial Example Defenses: Ensembles of Weak Defenses are not Strong, Warren He , James Wei, Xinyun Chen, Nicholas Carlini, Dawn Song, 2017
[5] Detecting Adversarial Examples Is (Nearly) As Hard As Classifying Them, Florian Tramèr, 2021
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper presents its key ideas in a clear manner.
content.summary_of_the_review: As mentioned in the weaknesses section, the paper does not present the general evaluation guidelines used for non-differentiable components (such as BPDA etc), or adaptive defenses that target the specific detection method of using data-depth. Given that most of the evaluations presented are with gradient-based attacks on the non-differentiable detector, these attacks are indeed extremely weak, and do not serve as an indicator of the true robustness achieved.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
